standard_prerequisites.name: The affine criterion for an open ring map in terms of going down for specializations, together with the translation between going down and the lifting of generalizations for the corresponding morphism of spectra, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the affine case of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: The reduction of a statement about a single specialization to an affine chart containing the two relevant points, using that the specialization of the image point stays inside an affine open containing the image
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the proof assume both schemes affine without losing the specializations involved.

core_obligations: Set up the specializations: start with a specialization of points of the target and a point of the source above the bigger one, and choose affine opens in source and target with the first mapping into the second and containing the relevant points (proof lines 4531-4536).

Reduce to the affine case: the specialization of the image point lies in the same affine open of the target, so replacing the schemes by these affine opens preserves the situation and the claim becomes the affine statement (proof lines 4536-4537).

Conclude: in the affine case the statement is the algebraic going down criterion for an open ring map, and the universal version follows by applying the result to base changes, which are again open (proof lines 4537-4542).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an affine chart containing the points involved, quote the algebraic going down criterion for open ring maps, and apply the same to base changes for the universal statement (proof lines 4531-4542).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that an open morphism of schemes lifts generalizations, and that a universally open morphism does so after every base change (statement lines 4518-4529). The counted proof is short and complete: it reduces a given specialization with a chosen point above it to affine charts containing the relevant points, where the statement becomes the going down criterion for open ring maps, and the universal version follows because base changes of an open morphism are open (proof lines 4531-4542). It is H2: the reduction and both conclusions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited input being the affine going down criterion.
